messages:
Jess: Quick follow-up on the canary/fallback convo from the RFC — I sketched a telemetry-driven gate + TTL fallback flow. Want feedback on tradeoffs before I turn it into a proper PR.

Rishi: +1. High level?

Jess: Idea: each rollout has 3 runtime-enforced primitives:
  1) gate: a set of metric predicates (p95 latency, error_rate, model_quality_drop, cost_delta) evaluated over a sliding window
  2) probe-oracles: lightweight probes (health, smoke gen, eval prompts) used to augment noisy production metrics
  3) fallback-ttl: when a gate trips, a deterministic fallback is applied for a TTL (e.g. 5m) before re-evaluation — prevents flip-flopping

Mira: How do we compute model_quality_drop in prod? we can't run full eval for every request.

Jess: Good q — plan is hybrid: sample X requests (configurable per rollout) and run them through a small eval set + automatic checks (length sanity, hallucination heuristics, perplexity delta). Then aggregate into a signal (noise-tolerant).

Dan: Need to ensure alerting and on-call semantics. If a gate trips and fallback happens, we should emit a distinct alert + include cause labels (latency|errors|quality|cost) so SRE can triage quickly.

Leah: Infra note: fallback-ttl interacts poorly with autoscaling. If fallback routes to a smaller infra plane, we might underprovision when we re-open. TTL window needs jitter and a probe-driven warmup step before full traffic resumes.

Rishi: Implementation-wise, router needs a simple contract: given request metadata + rollout state => route decision. We should keep decision logic deterministic and small. The control plane can push rollout policies (gate predicates, TTLs, probe configs) to routers as versioned blobs.

Mira: For A/B experiments we also want per-variant evaluation. Gate predicates must be variant-aware and compare baseline vs candidate. Can we avoid double billing when we mirror traffic for eval?

Leah: Mirror vs sample distinction: mirror = send read-only copy to candidate infra (no billing for output) where possible; sample = actually route N% to candidate (billing). We should prefer mirror for heavy models or when cost_delta is a gating signal. Depends on infra support.

Rishi: Edge case: cold-starts. A new variant may look bad on latency/error for first few minutes due to cold cache/KV warms. TTL helps but we also need a startup grace window and separate startup probes.

Jess: Proposed timeline:
  - startup grace: 2m after infra reports ready => hold off gate evaluation for this variant
  - probe-driven warmup: run synthetic gen probes and KV priming; only after probe pass do we allow traffic > baseline sampling
  - fallback-ttl: 5m default, configurable per rollout

Dan: Metrics to instrument (minimal):
  - per-variant request_count, p50/p95 latency, error_count, stream_abort_count
  - sampled eval_score (n samples/min) with score distribution
  - cost_per_token delta vs baseline
  - fallback_count and fallback_reason label

Mira: For model_quality we should publish an eval schema: prompt_id, baseline_score, candidate_score, metric_name, sample_ts. That makes it easy to compute rolling deltas and alert thresholds.

Jess: Agreed. Also want an RFC for a small rollout policy DSL so product can express: sample_rate, mirror, gate predicates, ttl, startup_grace, probe_config. Rough draft:```
rollout v1 {
  sample_rate: 0.02
  mirror: false
  startup_grace: 120s
  gate {
    p95_latency < 300ms over 5m
    error_rate < 0.5% over 5m
    eval.delta_score > -0.02 over 10m
  }
  fallback_ttl: 300s
  probes {
    smoke_gen: 10/min
    kv_prime: true
  }
}
```

Rishi: That DSL looks good. Router needs a compact serialized version (protobuf) and a simple state machine: STARTUP -> OBSERVE -> GRADED -> FALLBACK. Keep transitions idempotent.

Leah: Operational constraint: keep rollout control-plane load low. We'll push policies on change; routers must evaluate gates locally using pre-aggregated metrics. Control plane should only store policy history and ingest summarized telemetry, not raw per-request.

Dan: Also think about audit + explainability: when fallback happens we should attach a short reason string to returned error/headers so clients can react (e.g., X-Redwood-Fallback: latency_p95). Must be safe re PII.

Mira: One more: quality regressions can be subtle. Suggest a slow-burn rollback path: if eval score delta is small but trending down, schedule an incremental reduction of sample_rate (e.g., 50% -> 25% -> 0) rather than an immediate full fallback. TTL semantics and trend detection cover that.

Jess: Open questions for the group:
  1) Default TTL and startup_grace values? (ops-friendly but not too long)
  2) How many eval samples/min is realistic for high-throughput customers? cost tradeoffs?
  3) Should router compute metrics windows or rely on aggregated metrics from a local agent?

Rishi: My take: defaults: ttl 300s, startup_grace 120s. Router-local aggregation for short windows (1-5m) works best; longer windows come from metrics stack.

Leah: eval samples: start with 1-10/min per variant (configurable). Mirror for expensive models.

Dan: Add to runbook: if fallback_count spikes -> auto-create incident with rollback suggestion + link to recent probe failures.

canary-bot: probe_result variant=canary1 pass=false probe=smoke_gen latency=620ms time=1746001270

Rishi: ^ that shows why we need probe labels in alerts.

Jess: Action items:
  - Jess: draft rollout policy PR w/ DSL + examples (due EOD Thurs)
  - Rishi: proto for policy + state machine doc (due Mon)
  - Mira: eval schema + sampling recommendation (due Mon)
  - Leah: infra note on mirror vs sample and warmup primitives (due Mon)
  - Dan: runbook + alert mappings (due Tues)

Mira: Fine with that. Also adding a short checklist for experiment owners to set sensible sample rates and mirror flags.

Rishi: I'll add deterministic simulation tests for the state transitions so we don't get flappy rollouts.

Jess: Thanks all — will post the PR when draft ready. :thumbsup:
